bifrost: springboard/ui/src/extension.rs (points, identities, registry), springboard/core/src/extension_process.rs (process table, in-memory connections), springboard/sdk/src/extension.rs (app-facing re-exports and manifest text)
summary: Points, identities, discovery of enabled extensions and a process table with in-memory connections are built as pure models. The shell does not yet scan installed packages into the registry or start extension processes, and apps have no connection handler, so extensions cannot run yet.

features.feature: Adding support for app extensions to your app
features.apple: Create an app extension model by defining extension points and communicating with app extensions at runtime
features.note: Points, identities and the registry exist as pure data. No app calls them at runtime and the shell does not load them from packages yet

features.apple: Declare extension content and handle incoming XPC connections
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/extension.rs (manifest text), springboard/sdk/src/control.rs (per-app socket, not an extension entry point)
features.note: An extension can declare its identity in a manifest. There is no connection handler type, so an extension cannot receive connections from a host

features.apple: Find available extensions that match a host's extension points
features.note: Matching by point, enabled flag and name order are tested. Installed packages are not scanned, and no change stream reports availability updates

features.apple: Host launches an extension in a separate process and connects to it
features.bifrost: springboard/core/src/extension_process.rs (ProcessTable); launcher that starts apps: springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs
features.note: Process reuse per bundle and point, launching and running states, and connections with ordered queues are modelled. The table starts no OS process; the shell launcher has to report running and exit

features.apple: Declare a host's extension points and bind extensions to them, with scope rules
features.note: Declaration is checked against the owner's namespace, and scope is any or same developer. No user-interface or enhanced-security attributes, and no ExtensionPointDefining equivalent

gaps: Shell reads package manifests into the extension registry at login, on install and on removal
Shell launcher starts an extension process for a host request and reports running and exit to the process table
Connection handler type: an extension receives host connections through a closure, as the SDK's control socket does for apps
Share-sheet extensions installed by apps: the share menu does not read the registry yet
Extension point attributes (user interface, enhanced security) and an availability update stream
